Test the association between a trait and the environment

Source: R/phylo_gradient.R
fourth_corner_test.Rd

Weighted correlation between a site predictor and the mean of a species trait in each site, which is the fourth-corner statistic in the form of Peres-Neto et al. (2012). Permuting sites tests the link between composition and the predictor, and permuting species tests the link between composition and the trait. The association needs both, so the p-value to report is the larger of the two (ter Braak et al. 2012).

Usage

fourth_corner_test(comm, trait, env, n_perm = 999, site_permutations = NULL)

Arguments

comm

Matrix with one row per site and one column per species. Every site needs at least one individual.

trait

Numeric vector with the value of each species. Species are matched to comm by name, in any order, and those in only one of the two are dropped with a warning.

env

Numeric vector with the value of each site.

n_perm

Number of permutations of sites and of species.

site_permutations

Optional matrix of site indices with one permutation per row, for example from torus_permutations(), to use instead of free permutations.

Value

List of class mc_fourth_corner with correlation, p_site, p_taxa and p_max.

Article and original code

The function TraitEnvCor of the supplement differs from Appendix A, and this function from both:

  • Appendix A stacks the two null distributions, adds one to the count and uses alpha / 2. The code adds two to the count. Here we use the larger of the two p-values. The stacked p-value is close to their mean, so any test that it rejects at alpha / 2 is also rejected by the larger p-value at alpha.

  • Appendix A says that the statistic is calculated again for the permuted data. The code keeps the observed mean and standard deviation of the permuted variable, which then no longer has weighted mean zero. Here it is standardised again, as the code of the partition does.

  • The code runs n_perm - 1 permutations in each null distribution.

  • Appendix A allows several traits and predictors. The permutations of the code work with one of each, as here.

  • The code returns the absolute value, and here the correlation keeps its sign.

References

Peres-Neto, P. R., Leibold, M. A., & Dray, S. (2012). Assessing the effects of spatial contingency and environmental filtering on metacommunity phylogenetics. Ecology, 93, S14–S30. doi:10.1890/11-0494.1

ter Braak, C. J. F., Cormont, A., & Dray, S. (2012). Improved testing of species traits–environment relationships in the fourth-corner problem. Ecology, 93, 1525–1526. doi:10.1890/12-0126.1

Examples

set.seed(1)
env <- runif(40, 0, 100)
trait <- setNames(runif(15, 0, 100), paste0("sp", 1:15))
comm <- outer(env, trait, function(e, t) exp(-(e - t)^2 / 800))
colnames(comm) <- names(trait)
fourth_corner_test(comm, trait, env, n_perm = 99)
#> <mc_fourth_corner> trait-environment correlation
#> correlation: 0.7 
#> p (sites): 0.01  p (species): 0.01  p (max): 0.01
